summary_paragraph: Mrs. ___ was admitted for acute nausea, vomiting, and profuse green watery diarrhea, with a concurrent history of worsening shortness of breath and cough. Imaging revealed a new right upper lobe infiltrate consistent with pneumonia, treated with intravenous levofloxacin. A CT scan showed malposition of her GJ tube, with the jejunal limb pulled back into the stomach, contributing to her gastrointestinal symptoms. The tube was successfully replaced via interventional radiology. Diarrhea resolved after holding and then restarting tube feeds at a slower rate. She improved clinically, with resolution of respiratory symptoms and stable chronic pain management. She was discharged home with services on a 10-day course of levofloxacin, with plans for outpatient GI follow-up for esophageal stricture and continued management of chronic conditions including asthma, hypertension, and rheumatoid arthritis.
